subject: Data retention exception follow-up / FinAnalytics
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@finanalytics.com>, Bob Jensen <bob.jensen@finanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Data retention exception follow-up / FinAnalytics

Hi Alice / Bob,

Great to meet you on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on the data handling points you raised:

- You asked for no retention of user request/response content that contains PII ("0-retention") unless required for billing or legal reasons.
- You also called out audit/logging requirements: minimal operational logs for troubleshooting, and strict access controls + retention limits.
- Data residency: EU region preferred for production; trial can run in us-west.

Proposed short-term approach we can take while legal reviews:
1) We can enable request/response non-persistence (no stored input/outputs) for your test org.
2) Keep operational logs for 7 days for debugging, with automatic redaction of detected PII.
3) Provide downloadable audit log exports on request (we can add 90-day exports if needed via support).
4) Offer private VPC/dedicated tenancy as an option for guaranteed isolation.

Next steps: Can you confirm which fields you consider PII (or share a sample schema), and confirm whether 7-day operational logs are acceptable as an interim compromise? If so we'll loop in Legal and send an updated DPA+DPA addendum.

Attachments: FinAnalytics_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (your submitted questionnaire)

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@finanalytics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Jensen <bob.jensen@finanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception follow-up / FinAnalytics

Thanks Camila  good recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Our compliance team is asking for 0-retention for any request/response content that contains PII. In practice that means we cannot have any persistent logs of user inputs or generated outputs that include names, SSNs, account numbers, or any data that would identify a person.
- We understand operational logs are necessary for debugging, but we need them minimized and redacted. Would 0-retention for request/response + 90 days for audit logs be possible?
- Data residency: Production must be EU. Trial in us-west is acceptable for now but we need a timeline for EU cutover.

I attached a short list of the fields our compliance team considers PII  happy to share a schema offline if helpful. 

Next: Please send the DPA with the retention language and any proposed addendum for 0-retention. If legal needs to propose counter-language we can review quickly.

Best,
Alice Nguyen
Head of Security & Compliance | FinAnalytics
alice.nguyen@finanalytics.com
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@finanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception follow-up / FinAnalytics

Hi Alice  thanks for the quick reply and the PII list; that helps. A few notes and a proposed path forward from the product/ops side: 

- Zero-persistence (no storage of input/output) for PII-containing requests: we can enable a config for your org that prevents request/response material from being written to long-term storage. This is compatible with our hosted offering for trial orgs; for guaranteed enforcement in production we recommend dedicated tenancy / private deployment.

- Operational and audit logs: to balance debugging needs and your compliance ask, our standard offer is 7-day operational logs with automated PII redaction. For audit/papertrail needs we can provide an export process that preserves an immutable record for up to 90 days on request (exports are delivered over secure transfer and then removed from our staging area).

- Data residency: we can guarantee EU residency for production (we have eu-west regions). Migration timeline depends on capacity but we can prioritize your org once contract is signed F typical cutover 2-4 weeks.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v2.docx (proposed with retention clauses), audit_log_sample.csv (example, PII stripped).

If that approach is acceptable to FinAnalytics as an interim compromise (0-retention for request/response + 7-day redacted ops logs + 90-day export option), I'll get Legal to add explicit language to the DPA and prepare a DocuSign package. Looping in Marissa from Legal to propose contract language.

Thanks,
Camila

On 2026-06-20 13:42, Alice Nguyen wrote:
> Thanks Camila  good recap. A few clarifications from our side: ...
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@finanalytics.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception follow-up / FinAnalytics

Hi Alice / Camila  looping in Legal. Appreciate the clarity on the PII set. A few legal/contractual notes and a suggested compromise we can document in the DPA addendum: 

1) We can accept a 0-retention requirement for request/response data containing PII provided the customer agrees to the following controls:
   - Customer will attest that data required for billing or legal holds will be excluded from the 0-retention flag, or will notify Redwood of any legal hold requirements.
   - For debugging incidents Redwood will be allowed to create ephemeral snapshots (with PII redacted) for up to 7 days; these snapshots will be logged and access-controlled.

2) For audit and compliance purposes we can provide an export process that allows FinAnalytics to receive up to 90 days of audit logs on request. These exports will be delivered over a secure channel and will be the customer's responsibility to store. Redwood will not retain exported copies beyond 7 days.

3) Data residency commitment: we will include a clause guaranteeing EU processing for production if the customer executes the Private/Reserved capacity addendum or selects our EU-hosted dedicated capacity.

Operationally, Camila's proposed technical plan (0-retention flag + 7-day redacted ops logs + on-request 90-day export) is acceptable to Legal as long as the DPA addendum includes the above controls and customer obligations.

Action items for FinAnalytics: please confirm whether you can accept the customer-side obligations above (notably the legal-hold exception and responsibility to store exports). Also provide the procurement contact so we can route the DocuSign.

If you accept, we will:
- Insert the addendum language into Redwood_DPA_v2.docx
- Send DocuSign (DPA + addendum + SOW for EU cutover timeline)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@finanalytics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Jensen <bob.jensen@finanalytics.com>, procurement@finanalytics.com
Date: 2026-06-20T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception follow-up / FinAnalytics

Thanks Marissa / Camila  that sounds reasonable. We can accept the customer obligations you've outlined: we will notify Redwood of any legal-hold needs and store any exported audit artifacts. 7-day redacted operational logs + 0-retention for request/response with the legal-hold carveout is acceptable as an initial production configuration.

Please proceed with the DPA addendum and DocuSign. Procurement contact: procurement@finanalytics.com. We'd like the EU cutover scheduled within 3 weeks of signature if possible  can you include an estimated timeline in the SOW?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alice
Head of Security & Compliance | FinAnalytics
alice.nguyen@finanalytics.com
